# The Depth Mark: full text

> The Depth Mark is an independent digital studio that designs and builds award-level websites with motion, and adds SEO, answer engine optimisation (AEO) and AI automation so brands get found, chosen and remembered.

Website: https://thedepthmark.com/
Contact: https://thedepthmark.com/contact/

## Services

### Brand & Strategy

Positioning, identity and messaging that give your site something worth saying before a pixel moves.

### Web Design

Editorial layouts, bold typography and interaction design, shaped in Figma and proven in the browser.

### Motion & 3D

Scroll stories, micro-interactions and real-time WebGL scenes that make every visit feel directed.

### Creative Development

Hand-built front ends on Next.js, Webflow or custom stacks that load fast and hold up on every screen.

### AI Automation

Chat assistants, lead routing and content workflows wired into your site, so it keeps working after hours.

### SEO & AEO

Technical SEO and answer engine optimisation that get you found on Google and cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews.

### Launch & Care

We monitor, refine and evolve every site after launch, so it keeps performing as your brand grows.

## FAQ

### Do we need a full brief before we talk to you?

No. Most clients come with a feeling that their site does not match their ambition. Our discovery turns that feeling into a clear creative direction, so you do not need a plan before you start.

### How fast can we see something real?

Usually within two weeks. We pick one key screen, design it, animate it and put a live prototype in your browser, so you can feel the direction before you commit to the full build.

### Can our team edit the site after launch?

Yes. We build on a CMS your team can use without us, whether that is Webflow, Sanity or a custom setup. Pages, posts and images stay easy to change, while the design system keeps everything on brand. Every template comes with a short recorded walkthrough, so new people on your team can pick it up in minutes.

### Will the motion slow the site down or hurt SEO?

No, we design for both. Animations are built with performance budgets, images and video are sized for every screen, and heavy 3D only loads when it is needed. Every page also ships with clean markup, structured data and fast load times, so Google and AI assistants such as ChatGPT can read it and recommend it. We check every page on real phones before launch.

### Are we locked in after the project?

No. You own the design files, the code, the accounts and the documentation. If you want to take everything in house or hand it to another team, that takes a handover call, not a negotiation.

### What happens after launch?

We stay close. Every launch includes thirty days of care: fixes, small refinements and a performance review once real visitors arrive. After that you can keep us on a monthly retainer for new pages, campaigns and experiments, or run it yourself with the guides we leave behind.

## Case study: Varga (Photography Portfolio)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/graphizo/

A fashion and still-life photographer whose pictures refuse to stand still, and a portfolio that finally moves with them.

Ines shoots for brands that would rather be felt than seen. We opened her site with a Trivision wall: twenty rotating vanes that turn her name card into her latest work.

Her old site was a grid of same-size thumbnails, so a magazine editorial looked as loud as a test shoot. Art directors skimmed it in seconds, and the motion work that wins her commissions sat behind a link nobody clicked.

## Case study: Rossi (Stylist Brand Site)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/radario/

An independent hair stylist in Milan with a loyal client book and no place online that looked like her work.

Sofia’s cuts are clean, modern and built to last. The site had to read like a fashion editorial, and still let a new client book a chair in under a minute.

New clients found her through friends and a busy Instagram grid, then had to send a message to ask about services, prices and free slots. Bridal enquiries arrived too late, and nothing showed the care behind every appointment.

## Case study: OneFin (SaaS Website)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/northbank/

A finance platform that unifies spending, payments, investing and forecasting, with a website that made it sound complicated.

OneFin does five jobs in one app. The new site had to explain all five in a single scroll, and make money management look calm, bright and under control.

Every product had its own page, its own style and its own jargon. Visitors bounced between them trying to work out what OneFin actually was, and the sign-up button sat under three screens of feature lists.

## Case study: Reels (Agency Website)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/radius/

A creator agency that turns real people into a brand’s best sales team, with a website that looked like every other agency.

Reels lives on TikTok, Reels and Shorts, so its own site had to move at the same speed. We built it like a feed: bold, colourful and impossible to skim past.

Their old site was a services list and a contact form. Brands could not see the creators, the results or the process, so every lead needed two calls before anyone talked about an actual campaign.

## Case study: SphereAI (AI Product Site)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/dashmark/

A generative AI platform for writing, coding and creative work, launching into a market where every product promises the same.

SphereAI needed to feel less like a tool and more like a place to create. We gave it a luminous glass-and-light look, built around one simple prompt bar.

The product could write, code and generate images, but the old landing page listed models and parameters. Non-technical teams, the audience SphereAI wanted most, left before they ever typed a prompt.

## Case study: Wilun (App Landing Page)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/cooperative/

A payments app that makes business finance simple, with a launch site that had to feel as easy as the product.

Wilun takes budgeting, investing and payments off spreadsheets. We designed a bright, playful site where cards fan out as you scroll, so every feature arrives one at a time.

Finance apps all look alike: blue gradients, stock photos and dense tables. Wilun’s early page blended straight in, and visitors could not tell what made it different or what it would cost.

## Case study: Helora (Wellness Website)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/maple/

A therapy and wellness practice that helps people find calm, with a website that felt more like a clinic than a safe space.

Starting therapy is a big step. We designed Helora to feel like a deep breath: open skies, soft motion and one clear way to book a first session.

The old site led with forms, prices and clinical language. People already anxious about reaching out had to dig for the services, the therapists and the thing they needed most: reassurance.

## Case study: NexGo (Healthcare Platform)

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/case-studies/leapyear/

A telemedicine platform connecting patients with real doctors in minutes, with a website that had to earn trust at first glance.

Healthcare online is a matter of trust. We gave NexGo a warm, editorial look, real faces instead of stock icons, and a booking path any patient can follow on a phone.

Patients did not trust a faceless app with their health. The old site talked about technology, hid the doctors and buried the price, so most visitors called the clinic line instead of booking online.

## Article: How AI is changing the way websites are built

URL: https://thedepthmark.com/blog/how-ai-is-changing-web-development/
Published: 2026-10-06

A year ago, AI in our studio meant a chat window in a browser tab. Today it sits inside almost every stage of a project, from the first research sprint to the last check before launch. It has not replaced the people who make the work. It has changed where their time goes.

Every new tool promises to change how websites are made. Most of them change one step. AI is different because it touches all of them at once: research, design, code, content, testing and the work that happens after launch. Here is what that looks like inside a real project, and what it means if you are about to commission a website.

### Research takes days, not weeks

Discovery used to mean reading every competitor site, every review and every support ticket by hand. Now AI does the first pass. It groups hundreds of customer comments into themes, maps the words people actually use and drafts a competitor overview in an afternoon.

The judgement stays with us. A model can tell you that customers mention price forty times, but it cannot tell you that the real problem is trust. We spend the time we save talking to more real people, not fewer.

### Design explores more directions

Early in a project we now explore far more routes than we used to. AI helps us sketch layout variations, rough imagery and copy drafts in minutes, so a workshop can react to twelve ideas instead of three.

What it does not do is decide. Taste, brand fit and the small details that make a site feel premium still come from designers who know the client and the audience. AI widens the funnel. People choose what goes through it.

### Code ships faster, and cleaner

On the development side, AI pair programming has changed the rhythm of a build. Components, tests and the repetitive parts that used to take a day are drafted in an hour, then reviewed line by line by a developer. The time we save goes into the parts that make a site memorable: motion, interaction and performance.

#### Where it helps most

- Writing and updating tests
- Moving content between systems
- Turning designs into first drafts of components
- Catching accessibility issues before a human review

#### Where we keep it on a short leash

Anything that touches security, payments or personal data. Generated code is a draft, never a deliverable, and nothing ships without a review and a test.

### Content is written for people and for machines

Search is changing too. More visitors now meet a brand through an AI answer before they ever see its website. That means content has to be clear enough for ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google’s AI Overviews to quote, and structured so they understand who you are and what you offer.

We call this answer engine optimisation, and it now sits next to classic SEO in every build. AI helps us test how a page is summarised and where it gets cited, so we can close the gaps before launch.

### Sites keep improving after launch

The work no longer stops at go-live. AI assistants answer visitor questions, route new leads to the right person and flag the pages where people drop off. Small automations keep content fresh, and reports arrive without anyone building a spreadsheet.

### What does not change

AI is a powerful tool, but a website is still a set of decisions: what to say, who to say it to and how it should feel. Those decisions need people who understand your business and care about the result.

For our clients the change is simple. Projects move faster, budgets go further and more of the time goes into the craft that makes a site worth remembering. If you are planning a new website and want to see how this works in practice, book a free call with the studio.
